neighbours.label: an intensifying adverb opening a compound adjective (ever-changing, well-developed, ever-more)
fire: Farmers face drought and ever-rising costs each year.
It struggles to match the ever-growing demand.
You should become a well rounded player.
Cities keep up with ever-shifting rules.
Her well-known essay has a well-argued thesis.
The ever-present fog hid the coast.
quiet: Farmers face drought and rising costs each year.
It struggles to match the growing demand.
You should become a skilled player.
Cities never keep up with shifting rules.
The well was deep, and the thesis was long.
Ever since the fog came, the coast has been hidden.

short: ever-, well- opening a compound adjective
